arg.accentCustom: A literal colour for the shared record's border.
arg.accepts: The value the zone's rule compares against — a drop is legal when `el.values.rank` equals it.
arg.access: The viewpoints that MAY see this subtree. Empty hides it from everyone; no atom at all shows it to every seat.
arg.action: WHICH verb a press means — a ref into the action registry, never a callback: a node travels into snapshots and over wires, and a function survives neither. Empty, the control emits nothing and `activate` refuses, which is the whole of "disabled" here.
arg.align: Where the picture sits when it does not fill the area — nine anchors, from `topLeft` to `bottomRight`.
arg.alignItems: And where it sits DOWN its cell: top, middle, bottom. The same move on the other axis.
arg.alignment: Where the border sits relative to the contour: 0 outside, 0.5 centred on it, 1 inside. At 0 a wide border hangs over the box the layout spaced from its neighbours — switch on `bounds` to see it.
arg.angle: Turn, in degrees, clockwise on screen. It ADDS UP along the chain: turn a hand and everything in it turns with it, and a child cannot un-turn its owner.
arg.animateMs: Replace the recipe's own span, ms. Absolute, where `rate` is relative — give both and they compose. `0` leaves the look the length it was written with.
arg.answer: Which choreography the gesture answers with. The gesture and its answer are separate things — the kit reports a finger, the game decides what it means. `shiver` stays put, `zBounce` leaves the DESK and lands (watch the shadow fall away), `yBounce` jumps up the SCREEN without leaving the felt, `slide` travels and stops, `launch` is gone.
arg.asleep: Show every control as declining to act. Not a flag on the node — the kit has no `disabled`: the press still reports, the handler says no, and this is what the player sees while it does.
arg.axis: The reflection line, in degrees. A parameter, not a preset per angle: 90 is a Y-mirror, 76 is a 76° one. A mirror recipe reads it; a content-swap ignores it.
arg.back: The down-side surface. Empty falls back to the front, so a turn never blanks the card and a token identical both sides needs no back.
arg.bakePolicy: The painter's own say, over what the tree asked for. **asked** passes no option at all — the kit's default, which is to ask each node for `Bakeable`. **all** and **none** overrule every node in the scene, and are the two dullest members of the family of predicates the option really accepts.
arg.bend: How far the middle of the run is pulled sideways, in units. Zero is straight — there is no switch between a line and a curve, only where the places are.
arg.bordered: Re-register the shared record with a border, or without one. Both cards follow, and neither box moves.
arg.bounce: Restitution, 0..1: how much speed a body keeps off a floor (a launch) or a wall (a slide). `0` sticks, `1` never loses any.
arg.bounceBy: How high the FIRST arc reaches, in root units. About half a card's height — a jump nobody can miss that still keeps the piece over the seat it belongs to.
arg.bounceMs: How long the whole jump lasts, ms. Long enough to read as a jump rather than a twitch, short enough not to be a wait.
arg.bounces: How many arcs fit in the span; each is smaller than the last. Two — the jump, and the small one it lands with. A third reads as a ball, not a piece.
arg.bounds: The field itself, edited whole. `start` is where the path begins and each entry of `segments` has a `to`; a curve adds the handles `c1` and `c2`. The way back to `start` is implied — a shape is a closed region, so the last side is not written. Units, never pixels.
arg.box: The box this element belongs to — a name it carries, not where it sits. A return-slot's rule compares it as `el.box`, and only the matching slot lights.
arg.by: The seats that MAY lift this subtree. Empty locks it to everyone — a fixed board element; no atom at all is the open desk.
arg.cameraTurn: The view's angle, in degrees clockwise. The turn goes around the camera's target, which is what makes a seat at the desk a literal: an angle and a point, not a mechanism. Applied when this number changes, so the slider does not fight the fingers.
arg.canFlip: Does the card carry `Flippable`? The menu's `Flip` item exists only while it does — the offer is derived from the capability, never written out beside it.
arg.canRoll: Does the card carry `Rollable`? Turn it on and a `Roll` item appears with no other change — which is the point: a menu grows by a capability, not by an edit.
arg.canTap: Does the card carry `Tiltable`? Its `Tap` item comes and goes with it. `tap` has no `perform` in the registry: it is a pure query, and what it does is the game's answer.
arg.cap: How an open line ends: `butt` at the end, `round` past it, `square` past it and flat. Visible on dashes.
arg.capacity: The number the capacity rule reads: a drop is allowed while the zone's own child count is under it. Set it to 0 and even the first one is refused.
arg.cardAngle: The turn the card starts at, in degrees, so there is always something for a rule to keep or throw away. Two fingers on the card turn it too.
arg.cardDrop: How a CARD leaves the hand. `settle` is the ordinary putting-down every page here started with — it eases to the seat the finger chose, the pop unwinding on the way, and nothing is thrown, so there is nothing to schedule and nothing to re-order first. `fall` is the drop proper: let go of at the hand's height, coming down under its own weight.
arg.cardShare: How much two CARDS must overlap before they are one heap with a handle under it, as a share of a card's own area. The ordinary rule of every stacking desk on the shelf: cards have to be ON each other to be a pile, and two cards a finger apart are two cards. `0` and anything that touches at all is one heap.
arg.cards: One entry per card, in tree order — the list is the count and each card's paint at once.
arg.carry: The carry style of a run in flight, by registry name. `rigid` co-rotates the whole run about the grab — a column stays one plank; `loose` turns each card about its own middle — the per-card look a horizontal hand wants. At zero lean the two are the same picture.
arg.castShadow: Whether the control lays a shadow, and which contour: the footprint it declared, or the silhouette it actually draws.
arg.catchable: May a die in flight be CAUGHT. The engine has no opinion: a hand that lands on a piece always wins — the throw ends where the hand closed on it, and the seat and face it was carrying are written there and then. Off, and the scene says no through `Motions.busy` — the shape a shared desk writes for a die somebody else threw.
arg.cellReach: How far past its own edge a square still takes a piece, in units. `0` is what a board IS: a piece is on the square it is over and there is no other answer. Raise it and the squares begin forgiving a near miss exactly as a hand's area does, and the board becomes a felt with lines drawn on it — a piece let go of between two squares is taken by whichever is nearer rather than by the one it is standing in. The whole difference between a board and a felt, as one number.
arg.pointReach: How far past its own edge a point still takes a checker, in units. `0` is a board: a checker is on the point it is over. Raise it and the points begin forgiving a near miss, as the magnetism page does.
arg.childCount: How many children the container is filled with. Zero is an empty container, not an error.
arg.children: The real children, one entry per node — edited as the list it is, not a count. Every id lands exactly as written; the area of a surface with no box of its own comes from these, and taking them all away leaves nothing to paint on.
arg.chipDrop: The same for a CHIP, and its default is the other one — which is the point of having both. A card put down on a felt IS a putting-down; a chip dropped on one is a thing landing.
arg.coatLevel: The creeping magnitude, 0..1 — a charge, a smoulder, a dim's strength, a mask's opacity. A field, not a record per value: `wash` at 0.3 and at 0.9 is one recipe. A broken number clamps to nothing rather than throwing.
arg.coatRecipe: Which coat, by registry name — `wash` a flat overlay, `ring` a stroke, `censor` a mask, `clear` nothing (but it stops an inherited cast). Empty is no coat. The recipes differ by the KIND of mark, never by value: a darken and a charge are one `wash` told apart by tint and level.
arg.coatTint: The coat's colour, by token — empty falls to the recipe's own. A team's hue would be a parametric `{token:"spin", param}` here, one name and a number for infinitely many colours; the picker offers the flat tokens.
arg.colliding: Let a piece say how much room it takes, so no two that both said so end up on the same spot. Off, nothing takes any room and the desk is the one from before the feature: dice land on dice. It is not a second code path — off is the same throw with every piece answering zero.
arg.columns: How many cells wide the grid is. Children fill it in reading order, left to right first — a partial last row keeps its columns rather than recentring.
arg.corners: How many corners the regular polygon has.
arg.count: How many cards are dealt. Zero is an empty hand, not an error.
arg.d: The `d` of an SVG path, pasted whole — out of Figma, Illustrator or an `.svg` file. Straight runs and cubics, in units around the node's centre; quadratics and the shorthands are converted, and `A` (the elliptical arc) is the one command not handled — a path using it comes back empty rather than quietly missing a piece.
arg.dashAdjust: SVG's `stroke-dashadjust`. `stretch` scales the period so a whole number of them fits the contour; `none` leaves it alone — and then the first and last dash meet at the start and read as one of double length.
arg.dashCorner: SVG's `stroke-dashcorner`. `dash` repeats the pattern per side so every corner carries a dash. It needs sharp corners: on a rounded or round contour there are no sides to split on, and it falls back to the plain walk.
arg.dashOn: Dash length, in UNITS. Absolute — stretch the box and you get MORE dashes, not longer ones.
arg.dealt: Whether the pack has been dealt into a row. Flip it and every card springs from the stack to its own seat, keeping its identity across the change.
arg.dieDrop: How the DIE leaves the hand, and it has a third way open to it: `roll`. A die let go of goes over — always, not only when it was thrown hard, because that is what a die is for and one that came down flat and lay there would be a counter. Its face changes as it travels and the last one is the result, shown while there is still a roll left to see it on. `toss` is `roll` with a condition: a die set down gently keeps its face, and goes over only when the hand threw it.
arg.does: The word this control reports when pressed, written into `values` — the kit never interprets it.
arg.driftX: Where each next card lands relative to the one under it, across. Thickness is position, not `z`.
arg.driftY: The same drift, down the screen. Negative climbs up-screen, the way a pile actually looks.
arg.dropping: Let a released piece FALL onto the desk instead of being put down on it — from the height the hand was holding it at, and at the rate the piece's own weight asks for. Off, a release is an ordinary putting-down again.
arg.endHead: And what stands at the far end. The two choose independently, which is the whole arrow family in two controls.
arg.endSize: And how big the one at the far end is.
arg.endSurface: And the record the one at the far end wears. The two ends need not agree with each other either.
arg.face: The card's surface, by registry token. One face is enough to read the tilt — a 1×1.4 card is unmistakably portrait upright and landscape tapped.
arg.faceSurface: The INNER face, by registry name. Given, the control is two nodes: one quad carries one stroke, and a ring outside a keyline is two.
arg.faceUp: Which side is up. Runtime state, not the atom's — the card is turned in play; the atom only holds the down-side surface.
arg.fanGapMax: The furthest two cards of a lifted HAND may be, in units. The comfortable step, taken whenever nothing else has an opinion.
arg.fanGapMin: The closest two cards of a lifted HAND may ever be, in units. A floor about comfort: below it cards stop reading as separate things. It gives way the moment a ceiling — the desk, or the fan's own width — disagrees.
arg.fanTilt: How far the OUTERMOST card of the fan leans, degrees. The arc is derived from this and the fan's width, so a wide hand is a shallow sweep and a narrow one a steep one. `0` is no arc at all: upright cards in a straight line.
arg.fanWideMax: How wide a lifted HAND may get, as a fraction of the DESK. `1` lets it take the whole width — a hand held out is a thing you are meant to read, and it is not bounded by the zone it came from.
arg.fanWideMin: How wide a lifted HAND must be at least, as a fraction of the DESK. A short hand told to fill a quarter of the desk opens past its comfortable step rather than huddling in the middle of a space it was told to fill.
arg.fill: A palette TOKEN for the layer's colour. A token follows the theme; switch dark/light above and watch.
arg.fillCustom: A literal colour instead of the token. Both are legal, and only the token follows the theme — that difference is what the palette is for. Clear it to go back to the token.
arg.fillOpacity: How see-through the layer is, 0 to 1. This is where a zone's faint ground comes from.
arg.fit: How the picture meets the area. `contain` shows all of it and leaves bars, `cover` fills and is clipped by the contour, `fill` distorts, `original` draws it at its declared size, `repeat` tiles that size, `fitX`/`fitY` follow one axis.
arg.fling: Whether a released pan keeps going. Off is a setting, not a missing mechanism: the view stops dead with the finger and not a pixel further.
arg.flingCap: The fastest a throw may be, in screen pixels per second. Without it a flick of the wrist sends the desk into the next county.
arg.flingDecay: How fast a throw dies. The step is `exp(-decay × dt)`, so the slide is the same at 60 Hz and at 120; a per-frame decay sends the very same flick four times as far on a fast screen.
arg.flingFloor: Below this speed there is no throw at all — that is a hand coming to rest, not a flick. It is also where a running throw stops.
arg.flingSmoothing: How much of the newest sample the speed estimate takes. Half, so one late frame cannot become the throw — a desk that occasionally rockets away on release is worse than one that never coasts.
arg.flip: Which turn, by registry name — `mirror` reflects the geometry and swaps nothing, `turnOver` reflects AND shows the back surface. Empty is `mirror`. What the turn DOES lives in the recipe, not the atom.
arg.flipEase: The turn's easing over its progress. `linear` is a physical rotation (constant angular speed, so the width follows |cos|); `easeOut` snaps over and slows on the far side.
arg.flipMs: How long a turn-over lasts, in ms — the squeeze to an edge and back. Its own clock, apart from the settle's: a slow deal can still have a crisp flip.
arg.flipping: A TAP turns over whatever it landed on. Off, a tap is just a gesture that went nowhere and the cards stay as they lie. A gesture that STAYED is not a tap and turns nothing — hold a card and it does not move.
arg.focused: The input wiring's runtime state: does focus stand on the focusable bar right now? On, the story wears the stock ring on it — the same coat a game wears on Tab. Never a field on the element.
arg.followDamping: The chase spring's resistance to its own speed. Below `2·√stiffness` it is UNDERDAMPED — the read of the finger's speed overshoots a touch and eases back, so the lean keeps a little swing after a stop; at or above, no overshoot.
arg.followStiffness: The chase spring's pull toward the finger. It does NOT move the run — a held thing rides the hand 1:1 — it SMOOTHS the pointer into a speed: higher reads the finger quicker and twitchier, lower reads it lazier. That speed is the lean and what a throw inherits.
arg.frame: Whose corner the lamp hangs in. `viewer`: the screen's — a shadow reads as height the same way from every seat, and the lamp orbits the desk as the camera turns. `world`: the desk's — physical, the fall turns with the camera. They differ only while a camera is turned.
arg.friction: The desk's grip on a sliding body, in units per second squared — how fast a thrown die or puck bleeds its speed to a stop. Never pushes through zero: stopped is stopped.
arg.from: Which contour falls on the desk: `footprint` is the bare box the piece stands on, `silhouette` the contour as DRAWN — corners and all. Today the two differ by the record's corner radius; the day a piece wears a real figure skin, the silhouette follows it.
arg.fromX: Where the run starts, across. In units, on the node's own origin.
arg.fromY: And where it starts, down the screen.
arg.front: The up-side surface — what the card shows face-up.
arg.gain: Multiplies the finger's speed into the throw's: `1` is honest, more makes a flick a fling. Below half a unit per second the release is a DROP, not a throw, and the die stays where it was let go.
arg.gap: How far apart the two controls sit, in units. The story places them by hand in a free layout, so this is a pose and not a layout's spacing.
arg.given: The face to land on when `outcome` is `given` — what a server would send. A face the die does not have is refused, loudly.
arg.grainAngle: The zone's rule for the TURN: `derive` takes what the arrangement says (no registered layout has an opinion about a turn, and for a grid that reads straight), `stamp` imposes the number beside it, `keep` lets the carried turn land. A registry name, not a switch — a game's own fourth answer is a `registerGrain` call.
arg.grainOthers: What everyone ELSE is shown of a card's side: `same` is an open desk, `back` a strict game where only the owner reads their hand, `opposite` a hand held outwards. Not privacy — the cards are in every picture; what differs is which side of them each seat sees.
arg.grainSide: The zone's rule for the SIDE: `up` and `down` are the stamps, named for what the OWNER sees — right even inside a zone that is itself turned over — and `keep` accepts the side that arrived.
arg.grainStamp: The number a `stamp` imposes, in degrees. Meaningless to a rule that reads none, which is why the row is only here while `stamp` is chosen.
arg.gravity: The pull of a throw DOWN THE SCREEN, in units per second squared — how quickly a launched card curves toward the floor. Nothing on the desk (a slide) feels it.
arg.gripMax: The most of the view's own scale the handle will take, as a factor of the size it has at zoom 1. Above it the tab stops growing, so it never dwarfs the very heap it is a handle for.
arg.gripMin: The least of the view's own scale the handle will take, as a factor of the size it has at zoom 1. Below it the tab stops shrinking, so it never becomes a speck you cannot hit. `1` with `gripMax` at `1` is a handle that never changes size at all.
arg.gripMiss: How far a finger may MISS the tab and still take it, in units — the picture does not change. A control is aimed at with a fingertip and drawn for an eye: the tab is a few pixels tall on purpose, one drawn as a slab would be a slab, and a fingertip covers forty-odd pixels of glass while hiding the target on the way down. The answer is not to draw it bigger. It never steals: what is drawn is offered first, and only touches that would have found nothing at all reach this. `0` is the desk before this number existed.
arg.gripWidth: How wide the handle's tab is, in units. Its height follows by a fixed ratio: the SHAPE is what makes a tab read as a tab, and one that changed proportion with its size would stop being the same control.
arg.handCards: Cards in every hand. A hand is an ordinary container with an ordinary row in it; what makes it a secret is one atom listing who may look.
arg.head: Which head this is, by registry name. The stock four are geometry; a fifth is a `registerHead` call with any closed shape behind it.
arg.heap: The pile the odd chip out claims to belong to. Its own denomination, or its neighbour's — and the desk decides what heaps with what by comparing those names and nothing else.
arg.held: What it wears while it is held down. The only state a finger sees, so it carries the whole feedback.
arg.heldShare: How much of a card must lie INSIDE the zone before the zone counts it as its own, as a share of the card's own area. Its own number, and not the pull: the pull is about a MOMENT — the instant a hand lets go, and how generous the desk is about where — and this is about a STATE, asked of everything on the felt whenever anything moves. A card can end up in somebody's area without ever having been handed over — pushed there, knocked there, left half across the border — and the zone's handle takes it just the same, because a player looking at the desk would call it theirs.
arg.holding: Let what is already lying on the desk HOLD ITS PLACE when something is merely put down beside it. It stays solid, so nothing comes to rest on top of it — it is simply not shoved by a piece that only fell. Something genuinely travelling arrives and it is an ordinary body again, and goes skidding. Off, everything that gets in the way is shoved however gently it was let go, which is the neighbouring desk, Collision.
arg.hover: What the control wears while a pointer is over it. A mouse's answer — a finger never sees this state at all.
arg.id: The node's name. A node is named from outside; the tree below follows whatever you type.
arg.image: A registered picture for this layer, on top of its colour. Empty means the layer is colour alone.
arg.index: Which stop the card rests on now. Runtime state, not the atom's — the card is tapped in play. Past the ends it clamps into the list, so it can be dragged too far and the card simply holds on the last stop.
arg.innerR: The circle its notches come back to. Close to `outerR` gives a cog; far from it, a spike.
arg.inputPan: May the HAND move the view. A rule may close it in the middle of a game — a puzzle that pins the desk for its last move — and nothing is rebuilt: the wiring asks the camera at every gesture.
arg.inputRotate: May two fingers turn the desk. Closed by many games on purpose — a board with a right way up has nothing to gain from a twist.
arg.inputZoom: May the hand zoom. Closed, the wheel is not taken from the page either: a canvas that swallows it while refusing to move reads as a hung site.
arg.inset: How far the inner face sits inside the outer plate, in units. The ring is what shows between them.
arg.join: How two segments meet: `miter` sharp, `round`, `bevel` cut off.
arg.justifyItems: Where a child sits ACROSS its cell when the track is wider than it: left edge, middle, right edge. Moves the card within the cell only — the tracks hold still.
arg.keenLevel: The aim coat's magnitude, 0..1 — the same field the willing coat has, read by the same recipe. Two coats and one scale: a zone that answers both questions differs by strength as often as by kind.
arg.keenRecipe: Which coat the zone wears while the hand is OVER it, by registry name — empty and it says nothing about aiming, which is what every zone said before this field existed. A zone may also do the opposite: nothing for being merely willing, and its whole light for being the one that takes it, which is the honest answer on a desk with one zone.
arg.keenTint: The aim coat's colour, by token — empty falls to the recipe's own. Worth a different one from the willing coat: `may go here` and `will go here` are two sentences, and a reader has to be able to tell them apart at a glance.
arg.keeps: What the zone lets a child inside it keep doing: no atom is the open door, `["drag"]` lets a card leave freely but not act otherwise, an empty list is the closed case — nothing beyond what a bare capability already does on its own.
arg.keyHold: How much of the span the card WAITS out there, as a fraction. A pause is two keys with the same values — there is no `hold` field in a table, because a segment that changes nothing already is one.
arg.keyLift: How far the key carries the card off its seat, root units. Negative y is up the screen. It is an OFFSET, not a place — the same table plays the same anywhere on the desk.
arg.keyScale: How big the key makes the card, about its own centre. `1` is the size it rests at.
arg.keyTurn: How far the key turns the card about its OWN centre, degrees.
arg.kind: Which die: `d4` (a tetrahedron — a triangle from above), `d6` (the cube — pips), `d20` (the icosahedron — a hexagon with a numeral). The kind names the sides, the silhouette and the skin's faces.
arg.knock: What a die gives back off ANOTHER die, 0..1. Its own number and not the desk's: felt, rail and a second die are three materials, and one number for all three is a desk where everything is made of the same thing. `1` and they leave each other as fast as they met; `0` and they simply refuse to overlap.
arg.label: The caption, already written in the viewer's language. The kit paints no strings — whoever draws text (a HUD widget, the tree panel) reads this field.
arg.landing: Draw the picture of where a lifted run will land — a dashed silhouette on the felt, the shape of what will be lying there when the hand lets go. Off, and a lifted thing says nothing about where it is going: the desk before this feature, and worth turning off once to feel what carrying a hand across a board was like without it. What is lifted is in the AIR, and the air is not where it lands — so the cards, held clear of the finger and splayed, are the one thing that is not where they will come down.
arg.latency: One way, in milliseconds: a round trip costs it twice — once for the move to reach the shared board, once for the echo to come back. `0` is the honest default; the delay is a thing you turn ON, and with it up the split between what your own screen predicts and what the board has actually agreed becomes visible.
arg.launched: The trigger of a throw down the screen: flip it and the card is launched with the speed, heading and spin below, falls under `gravity`, bounces off the bottom edge and, once off the glass, eases home.
arg.layout: The arrangement, by registry name. Under `free` every child keeps its own `at`; under `row` the layout writes `at` for each of them — and nothing else: height, turn and scale stay the child's own.
arg.layoutName: The token this scene files its arrangement under — a node names a layout, it never holds one.
arg.leanDamping: The bank spring's damping. Under `2·√leanStiffness` the lean overshoots a touch as it swings through a turn; at or above it, no overshoot.
arg.leanFactor: How much horizontal SPEED becomes lean: degrees per unit/s of the chase spring's own velocity. The unit is the card, so this is degrees per card-width per second. `0` switches the whip off entirely; the lean saturates at `leanMaxDeg`.
arg.leanMaxDeg: How far the run banks into horizontal motion, in degrees at saturation. The lean comes from the chase spring's own speed and unwinds to zero at rest; `0` switches it off.
arg.leanStiffness: The bank spring's pull: how fast the run reaches the lean its speed is asking for. The lean is a spring of its own, not the speed itself — it saturates, so a hand that turns round would otherwise trade one pinned limit for the other in four frames, which reads as a snap rather than as weight.
arg.leash: How far past the wall (units) the finger may go before the HOLD breaks. A hand that keeps pulling on a piece which cannot follow is not holding it any more: the piece is left standing where it was.
arg.level: Where the knob sits, 0…1. The game's state too: a slider that remembered its own value would be a second answer.
arg.lift: The pop while held: the scale the lift spring plays from 1 when the run is grabbed, and back on release. `1` is no pop; a few percent reads as picked up without shouting.
arg.liftDamping: The lift spring's damping. Low, and the pop bounces once past `lift` before it settles; high, and it simply arrives.
arg.liftStiffness: The lift spring's pull toward the pop — how fast the picked-up run grows to `lift`. Snappier than the chase by default, so the pop reads before the trail.
arg.lifted: Raise the piece as the hand closes on it. Off, the hand holds it flat on the desk and the page is the one before this one — the height itself is `lift`, which is only worth showing while this is on.
arg.light.angle: Where the canvas's one light stands, in degrees clockwise from +x — the shadow falls exactly opposite. A ROOT field: turn it and every fall on the desk turns together, because no piece can bring its own lamp.
arg.lineAlign: Which edges line up ACROSS the line — `start` is tops in a row and left edges in a column, `end` the opposite, `center` the middles. Visible only when the boxes differ across; the walk along the line never moves.
arg.look: Which stock look the control wears: primary, quiet, danger, ghost. A registry NAME, not a sort — a fifth look is one registerSurface call in your own file.
arg.mark: Which action mark is attached to this piece — a record from the mark registry (`lifted`, `moved`, `captured`, etc.).
arg.maxZoom: How far in. The whole world scales, so the ratio between a piece and its shadow never changes: height is `z`, never a consequence of how close the camera is.
arg.mergeReach: How far a GATHERED piece looks for its own kind, in units. Its own number and not the share, because it answers a different question: the share asks how much of a piece is COVERED, this asks how far away another one still counts as NEXT TO it. Cards get none of it — a card has to be covered — so turning this to zero makes every pile on the desk a card's kind of pile, which is the honest way to see what the reach buys.
arg.mergeShare: How much of a piece must lie under another before the two are ONE PILE, as a share of the piece's own area. Below it they are two things that happen to overlap: a card that skids to a stop with one corner over a deal is not part of that deal. `0` is the old rule exactly — anything of the same kind that touches at all is one heap. Measured the same way `showsEnough` is, and deliberately a separate number: a pile packed tightly enough to hide its lower cards would be one no card could ever be added to.
arg.minZoom: How far the desk may be pushed AWAY. Below the zoom at which the whole desk fits, it stops being scrollable and is centred instead — a desk smaller than the glass has no edge to be pinned against.
arg.miss: How far past its outline this node still catches a touch, in units. Sized for a fingertip and drawn for an eye, near misses are forgiven without drawing a slab.
arg.miterLimit: How far a sharp corner may extend before it is cut off. Only for `miter`.
arg.motionName: Which registered look to play. The stock names the kit installs, plus `yours` — the one this page writes from the numbers below. Nothing about the call changes between them: `animate(id, name)` is the whole of it, and an unregistered name plays NOTHING rather than something else.
arg.nudge: How far it moves while held, in units. Depth and displacement are two statements: a look may want either alone.
arg.offsetX: Move the shape across, in units, away from the node's origin — the point `at` places and a rotation will turn about.
arg.offsetY: Move it down the other axis. Together with `offsetX` this is how a shape drawn from its corner is brought onto its origin.
arg.onReject: Where a REFUSED drop leaves the element — the atom's one policy word. `home` flies it back to the seat it left, on the spring; `stay` strands it where the finger let go, and that seat is written into the tree as its new rest.
arg.onRelease: Where the angle lands when the fingers let go: `keep` it, fly `home` to the angle it stood at before they touched it, or `snap` to the nearest step. The opposite default from a drag's on purpose — nothing refuses a turn, so undoing it by default would make the atom useless for the case it exists for.
arg.order: The permutation as text — `3,1,2,0`: at each place, the CURRENT index of the child that stands there. Empty, and `seed` draws one; a text that does not name every child once is not applied (the row stands until it does).
arg.orientation: Whose axes this node's turn is measured in. `world` rides the chain like `z` does: the owners' turn is added. `viewer` is a TERMINATOR — the accumulated turn is not inherited at all, which is what keeps a caption readable on a tray somebody sat down sideways.
arg.outcome: Where the RESULT comes from — the one door with three sides. `seed`: every client sharing the seed lands the same face. `given`: the number below, as the server said, the test pins, the cheat wants. `rng`: the game's own chance (`Math.random` here).
arg.outerR: The circle the star's points reach, in units.
arg.over: The upper layer's colour token, or empty for a picture alone.
arg.overAlign: Where the upper layer's picture sits.
arg.overCustom: A literal colour for the upper layer.
arg.overFit: How the upper layer's picture meets the area.
arg.overOpacity: The upper layer's opacity. Lower it and the order below starts to show.
arg.ownTurns: Turns this card has of its OWN, on top of whatever its owner contributes. A number and not a switch, because `turns` SUMS along the chain and the sum is what decides the side: one more turn shows the back, two more show the face again — a thing a checkbox has no way to say.
arg.padding: Room left around the tight wrap of the content, in units, before the surface is painted. Zero shrinks the area to exactly that wrap.
arg.physics: Switch the carry's PHYSICS on. Off, a grabbed piece is nothing but the finger's position — no lift, no bank, no easing; on, it is the kit's own carry (`lift`, `leanFactor`, `leanMaxDeg`) as `DEFAULT_TUNING` has it. The position is not part of the switch: a held thing rides the hand 1:1 either way.
arg.picked: Which member of the segmented row is on. The GAME's state — the row is built from it, and holds no copy.
arg.pitch: How far the desk is laid back, in degrees — 0 is straight down onto it, 60 is a low seat. It is a squash along the screen's own vertical, so the whole view stays a plain matrix: the finger, the clamp and the painter go on working untouched. What it does NOT do is converge the edges — a desk drawn as one huge plate stays a rectangle rather than a trapezoid.
arg.placeable: Whether this node carries the marker. It draws nothing: what changes is the answer a slot gets when it asks.
arg.plateSurface: The outer face, by registry name. Absent, the control is invisible and still pressable — which is exactly what an invisible hit area is.
arg.points: How many points the star has.
arg.policy: The cell's own `Displacer` name for what happens to the sitter: `reject` refuses the incomer, `merge` leaves both, `capture` sends the sitter to the tray beside the cell.
arg.polyR: The circle the polygon's corners sit on, in units.
arg.preset: Which builder the shape comes from. Not a sort of `Shape` — there are none. Every choice but `path` is a helper function the kit exports, and the snippet shows the call; `path` is the raw value itself, printed as it stands.
arg.pull: How far the zone reaches past its own border, in units. A release inside that much of the edge still belongs to the zone, so a player aiming at their area does not have to aim at a pixel. `0` is every other desk: the release has to land inside the border. Turn on `bounds` to see it — the border swept by a disc of that radius.
arg.r: Radius, in units. A circle is stored as a radius and turned into a polygon on the way to the renderer.
arg.radius: Corner radius of the box itself, in units. Zero is a plain rect. This rounds the BOX — a layout and a finger see it; the surface record has a radius too, and that one rounds only what is painted.
arg.rank: The card's rank, written into `values` — the field the zone's rule compares as `el.values.rank`. Slide it through 7 and watch the verdict change; nothing else about the card moves.
arg.rate: Play speed as a MULTIPLIER — 2 is twice as fast, 0.5 half. Relative on purpose: a scene slows every look it plays without knowing how long any of them is. Zero is a mistake, not a still frame, and is read as ordinary speed.
arg.raw: Print the shape's VALUE in the snippet instead of the call that built it. Changes nothing on the stage — it answers "what does `rect(1, 1)` actually return", which no other page in the catalog does.
arg.reach: How far out this piece looks for its own kind, in units — measured from its outline, not its centre. At `0` it has to be COVERED to belong, which is what a card means by a pile: a hand is a hand because the cards are on each other, and two cards a finger apart are two cards. Above `0` it is a NEIGHBOURHOOD, and anything of its pile inside it belongs — which is what a chip means by a pile, and what dice mean by a roll. Nobody stacks dice; they are gathered. Turn on `bounds` to see it: the box swept by a disc of that radius, drawn around every piece that has one.
arg.recipe: How the reorder LOOKS, by registry name (`installStockShuffles`): `riffle` splits and zips, `overhand` lifts packets, `wash` scatters to a ring, `shake` trembles in place. The recipe never sees the seed; the seed never sees the recipe.
arg.registerAs: The token this scene files its record under — the node names it, the registry holds the record itself.
arg.retain: Keep what the glass shows and paint only what flies — nothing at rest is repainted, so a thrown card leaves its trail. The old solitaire's victory cascade. Off, the next frame repaints everything.
arg.rides: Does the shadow travel WITH the card (1) or wait at the seat (0)? Off, the card reads as lifted off the desk; on, as sliding along the felt. Same motion, same numbers — the shadow is the entire difference, and it is a property of what the look MEANS.
arg.right: Which slot the token rests at. Flip it and the node eases across on the one clock — the settle, watched with no drag.
arg.ringRadius: How far from the container's origin every seat stands, in units.
arg.roll.hop: How much the piece grows at the top of its hop, as a scale — `1` is flat, `1.25` a clear lift. The hop peaks at the middle of the tumble and is gone by the end.
arg.roll.turns: How many whole turns the piece makes about its own centre over the tumble. Whole, so it comes to rest upright — a fraction would leave it turned.
arg.rollMs: How long a tumble lasts, in ms — the turns and the hop of a die rolled in place. The face is committed late in it, when the piece turns slowest.
arg.rolled: The trigger of a tumble: bump it and the piece rolls again in place — turns and a hop on the clock — committing its result late in the roll.
arg.room: How much room a piece takes from another piece in ITS OWN world, as a factor of the piece's narrowest side. A factor and not a length, because three sizes stand on this desk and one number could only ever be right for one of them: at `1` two pieces of a kind come to rest edge to edge. The room is a disc, so a card measured across its width will let two cards overlap stacked end to end — measured by its height instead, two cards side by side could never come within a card's length of each other, which is not a desk anybody has played on.
arg.rotate: Turn the shape, in degrees. A turned rect is a polygon: a `rect` is axis-aligned by definition, so the sort that can still say the result is `poly`.
arg.rule: Which rule the ruled zone's `Acceptor` carries: the open door (`and: []`, welcomes everything) or a capacity read off the zone's own child count.
arg.rx: Half the ellipse across, in units.
arg.ry: Half the ellipse down. Equal to `rx` and it is a circle — that is all a circle is.
arg.said: Say it again. Every step of this counter fires the answer once — the same thing tapping the card does, for a reader who would rather drive it from the panel.
arg.scale: Size, as a multiplier. It MULTIPLIES along the chain — a half-size hand holding a half-size card shows it at a quarter, and no sum says that. One number, not two: a non-uniform scale is the only transform that destroys a shape, and squashing belongs to the picture.
arg.scaleX: Scale across, applied to the shape before it becomes `bounds`. This is AUTHORING, not a pose: what reaches the model is the shape with the number already baked in.
arg.scaleY: Scale down the other axis. Uneven with `scaleX` and a circle becomes an ellipse — which is a polygon here, because the model has no `ellipse` sort.
arg.scatter: How hard a handful pushes itself apart as it leaves the hand, units/s. Two dice let go of at the same instant take the same speed the same way, and physics has nothing to say about that — they travel as one and arrive as one. A hand does not close on a throw, it OPENS, and this is that: each piece its own heading, fanned about the throw, with its own push along it. It is also what makes a DROP scatter, where there is no throw to fan.
arg.screens: How many seats are watching this one board at once. Each screen is a projection of the SAME tree with its own camera — not a copy of the game, a copy of the view.
arg.screened: Whether this node maintains its size on the glass across camera zoom instead of scaling with the world.
arg.screenMax: The highest scale factor of its zoom-1 size this node will grow to.
arg.screenMin: The lowest scale factor of its zoom-1 size this node will shrink to.
arg.seat: Whose seat this canvas plays — the wiring judges picks and projections from it. Grip: your own hand's cards lift, the other seat's refuse. Privacy: your view holds your hand, the other seat's is simply not there.
arg.seed: The seed the kit's rng draws the order — or the face — from. The same seed gives the same result on every machine, which is how a shared desk agrees without being told; change it and the draw changes.
arg.settleEase: The settle's easing, by registry name. `easeOut` leaves quickly and arrives gently — the shape a card settling into a pile wants; `linear` is a constant glide. A game registers its own with `registerEasing`.
arg.settleHold: How long the card lies exactly where it landed before the zone's answer starts moving it, ms. The rest pose is the same either way — a hold changes only how long the desk takes to admit it. Zero with a zero travel is a snap: there on the frame it arrives.
arg.settleMs: How long a settle lasts, in ms — the glide of a node from where it is to the seat the tree now gives it. A field of the tuning: the same number the game hands `attachMotion`, and the header's speed multiplies it for the onlooker.
arg.shadow.base: How far a shadow falls from a piece RESTING on the desk (z 0), in units. Root field of the lamp: one depth scale for the whole desk. Zero, and a resting piece looks painted on.
arg.shadow.lifted: The extra fall of a piece in FLIGHT — carried, settling, turning — in units. It ends with the flight; the resting arithmetic never learns about it.
arg.shadow.opacity: How dark the shadow layer lies, 0..1. One ink for every shadow on the desk — a shadow is a layer of the lamp, not a picture of the piece.
arg.shadow.perZ: How much further the shadow falls per unit of resolved `z`, in units. Height is the source, the fall is its consequence — this is the exchange rate.
arg.shakeStrength: How hard the group is shaken. It moves both halves of the look at once: a harder shake trembles wider AND throws the pieces onto each other's seats oftener. `0` only trembles and never changes hands.
arg.shiverBy: How far it swings at its widest, in root units. Sized against a CARD — about one unit across — so this is a swing of some seven pixels on a phone. A third of it could not be seen at all: a 2-pixel swing lasting 180 ms is not a subtle animation, it is an absent one.
arg.shiverCycles: How many there-and-back swings fit in the span. Three in 180 ms is roughly the frequency a hand reads as a buzz.
arg.shiverMs: How long the tremble lasts, ms. Short enough to read as one event rather than as an animation: a twitch, not a wobble.
arg.showsEnough: How much of itself a card must SHOW to take the finger, as a fraction of its own footprint. A pile hides all but a sliver of what is under its top, and a finger landing on a sliver gets a card nobody was aiming at. Below this it does not answer at all: the touch goes to whatever is covering it, and so on up the pile. `0` is the plain answer — the topmost thing under the point, however little of it there is.
arg.shuffleMs: How long a shuffle's choreography lasts, in ms — from the first piece leaving its seat to the last one landing on its new one. The recipe shapes what happens inside; this is the whole span.
arg.shuffled: The trigger of a shuffle: bump it and the row shuffles again — to the order `seed + shuffled` draws — through the chosen recipe. The scene remembers the order it landed in between renders.
arg.sides: How many faces the piece can land on — 4, 6, 20. The atom's one field; the face itself is a VALUE (`values.face`), and the picture of a face is a skin's.
arg.sink: How deep it goes while held, in units. Written to z, so the cast shadow shortens by the plan's own arithmetic rather than by a second drawing.
arg.size: How big it is, in units — the shape is drawn once in a unit square and scaled from there.
arg.slideHop: How hard the throw takes the piece OFF the desk, units/s of rise. A thrown die does not skate — it bounces: it falls under the same gravity a launch uses, gives back `bounce` of every landing, and each touch-down turns its run a little, so it wanders instead of ruling a line; a wall throws it higher than the hop it was already on. The SHADOW is what shows the height — it rides under the piece and drops away as it rises. `0` is a puck, flat all the way.
arg.slots: The prepared places, in units on the container's origin — seat 1, seat 2, seat 3, taken in tree order. A child beyond the last slot keeps its own pose.
arg.snapStep: The grid a `snap` release lands on, in degrees. Read for nothing else. A step of nothing is not a grid, and is treated as `keep` rather than dividing the angle by zero.
arg.spinFriction: How fast a sliding body's SPIN bleeds out, in degrees per second squared. Independent of the slide's own friction, so a die can keep turning after it has all but stopped moving.
arg.spotDrop: How far below its own middle the spot sits, in units. A standing figure's shadow is at its BASE, not around its waist — and a spot left in the middle hides entirely under the figure, which reads as no shadow at all.
arg.spotWide: How wide a spot this lays on the desk INSTEAD of its own shape, in units. `0` and it lays its own, which is right for everything that IS its own shape — a star casts a star. It is not right for a piece whose picture is a DRAWING inside a box: the box is what falls, a rectangle a size the eye cannot match to anything, sitting under a figure it plainly does not belong to. The honest silhouette can only be TAKEN from the drawing, and nothing here reads a picture's alpha. So: a spot, which depicts nothing and therefore cannot depict the wrong thing — and never a hand-drawn outline 'of a figure in general', which gives the knight the pawn's shadow the day a second kind of figure arrives.
arg.sparkDrawn: The DRAWING that falls: instead of a contour, the spark lays a picture of itself in shadow ink — the honest silhouette of a drawn piece, the knight's shadow being the knight. Made the only way it can be: whoever drew the piece drew its shadow too; nothing reads a picture's alpha. `picture` on `ShadowCaster` names that asset.
arg.spotlight: Clear the cast on one child back to nothing. «All but this one» is a dim on the tray and a `clear` on the lit figure — the inversion is overriding an inherited value, not a scope switch.
arg.spread: The whole arc in degrees, first card to last. More cards pack the same arc tighter — the fan does not widen.
arg.stacking: Let touching pieces of one kind form a HEAP, with a handle under it that lifts the whole thing as one squared stack. Off, pieces that overlap are just pieces that overlap: no handles, and every finger lifts exactly what it landed on.
arg.stand: Whether the pieces stand up out of the laid-back cloth (`Oriented: "viewer"`) or lie on it with it (`world`). Per element and not a mode of the camera — the same field that keeps a caption upright over a turned slot.
arg.startAngle: Where the first child stands, in degrees clockwise from twelve o'clock — the same sense `angle` turns.
arg.startHead: What STANDS at the near end, by registry name — the end itself is `from`. Nothing is the ordinary case; a head at both ends is the arrow that points both ways.
arg.startSize: How big the head at the near end is, in units. Each end has its own — a dot where a run begins and a point where it lands is the ordinary case.
arg.startSurface: Which record the head at the near end wears. It is a node of its own, so it can be solid where the line is a hairline — or carry a picture. Empty means it wears the line's.
arg.stepX: The step between neighbours, across. Turn it sideways and the column becomes a dealt river.
arg.stepY: The step between neighbours, down the screen — far enough that every card's top stays readable.
arg.stops: The discrete tilt angles, in degrees clockwise, written as a list — `0, 90` is upright and tapped, `0, 120, 240` a three-way standee. The tap steps through them in this order; the length is the point, so it is a text field, not a slider.
arg.stroke: Draw a border. It is always last, over every layer — a border cannot be hidden by the thing it borders.
arg.strokeColor: A palette token for the border.
arg.strokeCustom: A literal colour for the border, winning over the token.
arg.strokeOpacity: How see-through the border is, 0 to 1.
arg.strokeWidth: Border thickness, in UNITS. Absolute: stretch the box and the border does not thicken.
arg.style: Which ROLE this caption is — the name of a registered text style, never a font. A role is what a tree can say and a designer can re-decide; the family and the size are the theme's answer. Empty is the desk's default face, and so is a name nobody registered.
arg.swap: Put the upper layer underneath. Order is the whole reason a record holds a LIST.
arg.sweep: The whole walk, first child to last, in degrees. The full 360 shares the circle evenly with no doubled seat at the seam; anything less is an arc taken end to end.
arg.text.family: The font stack, already written the way the platform expects it.
arg.text.fill: The ink, by palette token — one style reads correctly on both palettes without being written twice.
arg.text.lineHeight: Baseline to baseline, as a multiple of the em.
arg.text.size: Em size, in UNITS — never pixels, so one role is one size on every device.
arg.throw.angle: The heading, in degrees clockwise from +x on the screen — `0` is right, `90` down, `270` straight up. The kit's one angle convention, the same one the lamp uses.
arg.throw.speed: How fast the body leaves, in root units per second. A launch turns it into a flight under gravity; a slide into a glide the desk's friction eats.
arg.throw.spin: How fast the body turns while it flies, in degrees per second. A slide bleeds it by `spinFriction`; a launch keeps it to the end.
arg.throwing: Hand the finger's speed on to the released piece, so it keeps going and the border throws it back. Off, the piece drops where it stood: a throw is a drop with the hand's speed still on it, and this is that speed.
arg.thrown: The trigger of a throw across the desk: bump it and the body is thrown with the speed, heading and spin below, slows by friction, bounces off the tray's walls, and stops where it stops.
arg.tintToken: The parametric colour token the tiles paint with — a NAME the painter resolves; the seat is its number.
arg.toY: And where it ends, down the screen.
arg.trail: How far each piece of a carried run falls behind the one before it. `0` is a run carried as one plank — the stock feel. Above it the run stretches out behind the hand and closes up again when the hand stops, the way anything held by one end does. The FIRST piece is never late: it is what the hand has hold of.
arg.trayAngle: The TRAY's own turn, in degrees. It is the scene's knob, not a field of this atom — turn it and the chain both tokens inherit turns with it, which is the only way the difference between the frames becomes visible.
arg.turn: The angle it faces, in degrees. On a path this is read off the path; alone, it is yours to set.
arg.turnCap: The fastest the desk may spin, in degrees per second. A coast runs for about speed ÷ decay degrees, so this and the decay together say how far a hard flick carries.
arg.turnFling: Whether a released twist keeps turning. Off is a setting, not a missing mechanism: the desk stops at the angle the fingers left it at.
arg.turnFloor: Below this speed the turn does not coast — a hand settling, not a spin. Also where a running spin stops.
arg.turned: The trigger of a turn-over: flip it and the clock plays a `flip` on the card — squeeze to the edge, swap the side there, grow back. Not a description of the tree: the render tells the clock only when this changes.
arg.turns: How many turns from the authored state. It SUMS along the chain — a stack turned once turns every card once — and the current side is the PARITY: even is face-up, odd is over. Whole steps, because a turn is whole.
arg.under: The lower layer's colour token, or empty for a picture alone.
arg.underAlign: Where the lower layer's picture sits.
arg.underCustom: A literal colour for the lower layer.
arg.underFit: How the lower layer's picture meets the area.
arg.vertices: The path itself, as `x,y` pairs — the raw `Shape`, with no helper in front of it. Two pairs are a line, one is a point, and neither encloses anything. Every other preset on this page comes out as a value of exactly this kind.
arg.w: Width, in units. Not pixels — the host decides what a unit is worth on screen, so the same number is the same size on every device.
arg.wallBounce: How much of that speed comes back off the wall, 0..1 — the same restitution a slide's bounce is. `0` knocks it off and drops it; `1` sends it away as fast as it came.
arg.wallSpeed: The tray's wall while a FINGER is carrying the piece: how hard (units/s) it has to be shoved into the border before the wall wins and knocks the piece off the hand — it comes back off it, tumbling. Slower, and the piece just stops on the wall and goes on straining after the finger.
arg.washRadius: The radius of the ring the pieces scatter to, in units. `0` is auto — a ring that just clears the group, whatever size it is.
arg.width: The shared record's border width, in units.
arg.wrap: What a tap does at the end of the list. On, past the last stop it returns to the first — the card that taps and untaps; off, it rests on the last, a dial that stops at its end.
arg.wrist: How far below the cards the wrist sits, in units — the point the fan pivots about. Closer is steeper.
arg.x: Offset along X, in units, from where the node would otherwise sit.
arg.z: Height in the paint order. Whole steps: it is an order, not a distance, and it ADDS UP along the tree.
arg.zoneGapMax: The furthest two cards lying in the ZONE may be, in units — the comfortable step of the row.
arg.zoneGapMin: The closest two cards lying in the ZONE may ever be, in units. Same meaning as the fan's, measured in the same units, against the zone's own box instead of the desk.
arg.zoneTurns: Turns on the ZONE, not on the card. One turn is the closed deck: everything in it shows its back, and nothing was written to a single card — pull one out into an untouched zone and the face is there again.
arg.zoneWideMax: How wide the ROW in the zone may get, as a fraction of the zone's own box. The zone's border is a hard ceiling above this one: a row never leaves the place it is in, whatever these numbers say.
arg.zoneWideMin: How wide the ROW in the zone must be at least, as a fraction of the zone's own box.
arg.zoomCap: The fastest a zoom may coast, in natural logarithms of the zoom per second — `1` is "e times bigger every second". Without a cap a sharp pinch throws the desk to its limit in one frame.
arg.zoomFling: Whether a released pinch keeps zooming. The speed is kept in logarithms of the zoom, where a decay is symmetric — so coasting outwards dies exactly as coasting inwards does.
arg.zoomFloor: Below this speed the zoom does not coast at all — that is fingers coming to rest, not a flick. It is also where a running coast stops.
arg.zoomSensitivity: How hard one wheel notch zooms. The factor is `exp(-delta × this)`, a RATIO rather than an addition — so out and back lands exactly where it started, at any zoom.
inspector.noAtoms: none — an id and a place, and that is valid
inspector.title: node tree
scene.nothingDrawn: nothing is drawn: no atom here paints. The node tree is the scene.
viewer.bounds.hint: Outline every footprint. A box paints nothing on its own — this layer is the only way to see one.
viewer.grid.hint: Rule the view one line per unit — so a size can be read off the scene instead of taken on trust.
viewer.hudUnit.auto: Auto — a quarter of the shorter side
viewer.hudUnit.hint: The etalon this scene measures HUD sizes against
viewer.touch.hint: Ring the point every finger that is DOWN is read at — the anchor a gesture hangs off. What stopped a piece is the gap between the ring and the piece, and nothing else on screen shows it.
arg.handLock: Whether the bottom reader has shut their own hand. Shut, it takes nothing from anybody else and gives nothing up to them: a card let go of over it comes back, and a card lying in it cannot be picked up. Its own screen is unaffected — the lock is about everybody else. Either seat's own reader turns it by tapping their own disc; the knob is here so the state can be opened straight into.
arg.avatarPin: What your own picture is fastened to. `screen` pins it to a point of your own glass — the lower left corner — so it rides your view and travels the desk as you pan, which is what tells everybody else where you are looking. `desk` stands it on a spot of the felt instead, where it stays while the view moves over it, and then the leash decides what happens when the view walks off it.
arg.avatarLeash: What a desk-pinned picture does when your view leaves the spot it stands on. `lock` holds the CAMERA: pan far enough and the view simply stops, because your own picture has to stay on your glass. `chase` holds the PICTURE: the view goes wherever it likes and the picture is pressed against the border it went out through and slides along it, so you are never off your own screen. It says nothing at all about a screen-pinned one, which cannot be left behind.
arg.avatarBounds: Draw the outline of the other reader's view on this one — the four corners of their glass, taken to the desk through their camera and back through yours. A debug picture of the thing the avatar already says more quietly, so it is off by default.
arg.avatars: Whether the two people are at this desk at all. On, each of them is drawn ON the felt as a disc in their own colour, standing where their own camera says they are looking from — and at a card table each of them has a hand of their own standing beside them. Off, the desk is the felt and the pieces and nothing else: no discs, and no hands.
arg.idleReturn: Whether a view left alone glides back to this reader's own seat. Only means anything with `avatars` on — the seat the view returns to is the same place the disc stands at. Pan away and stop touching the glass: after the countdown the camera glides home on its own, and any finger back on it starts the countdown over.
arg.idleMs: How long a view may sit untouched before it starts gliding back to this reader's own seat, in milliseconds. Only means anything with `avatars` and `idleReturn` both on.
